newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index down at noon as HK hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index down at noon as HK hopes fade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended the Wednesday morning session more than one percent lower as investors lost hope of further gains on the back of the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, brokers said.
Volume was relatively thin with many investors sticking to the sidelines in the belief that the Hong Kong-related rally had finally run out of steam, they said.
The B share index fell 1.196 points or 1.41 percent to end the morning session at 83.748 points on volume of 4.933 million shares worth $3.080 million.
"The Hong Kong handover is a done deal," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "We've been expecting a bit of a dip and most clients are cautious."
Hong Kong reverts to Beijing's sovereignty at midnight on June 30.

Shanghai shares surged earlier this year on expectations that Beijing would want booming stock markets through the handover, but the meteoric rise caused government regulators to step in in May and bring prices down.

Investors refrained from buying on Wednesday on fears of more government measures to cool the market and in anticipation of Hainan Airlines' listing of 71 million B shares on Thursday, which will attract buying interest, brokers said.
Selling of real estate plays based in Shanghai's Pudong development zone also helped pull the market down, they said.

"The correction of real estate Pudong shares helped push the index down, but selling pressure was not heavy," one local broker said. "Investors just have little interest in buying due to the current weak market sentiment."
Of 44 B shares, 37 traded with 24 down, eight flat and five up.
Shanghai Vacuum And Electron Device Co. was the biggest B share loser, slumping $0.010 or 4.76 percent to $0.200.
Pudong-related share Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Co also performed poorly due to institutional selling. It fell $0.028 or 3.21 percent to $0.844.
Qingqi Motorcycle 900946.SS was the most actively traded on institutional profit-taking, losing $0.014 or 2.62 percent to $0.520 on volume of around 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai A shares also lost ground during the morning session on Wednesday due to investor caution and an expected flood of new listings, brokers said.
The A share index shed 2.173 points or 0.16 percent to close the morning at 1,360.694 points on volume of 210.3 million shares worth 3.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index edged down 3.085 points or 0.07 percent to 4,150.516 points.
Brokers said they expect the A and B share markets to continue to edge lower ahead of the Hong Kong handover as investors wait for new direction.
"I think investors are waiting for a clearer direction," said another local broker, who added the B index is likely to test support at 83 points in the short term.
